content:
At last night's Emmy Awards ceremony, Apple TV+ delivered an outstanding performance, beating out competitors like HBO to become the most-awarded platform of the night. Below is HBO's Casey Bloys' response to Apple TV+'s wins.

HBO's CEO praised Apple TV+'s impressive performance, while also acknowledging that competing with a company worth one trillion dollars is "quite challenging."

Apple TV+ has long been compared to HBO, as both prioritise quality over quantity. Apple has even occasionally been dubbed the "new HBO."

Last night's Emmys further cemented that notion, with Apple TV+ surpassing HBO, Netflix and other platforms to become the most-awarded platform of the night.

Apple TV+ swept a total of 29 awards, earning the honour of "most-awarded network of the year," with shows like Widow's Bay performing particularly well. HBO followed closely behind with 21 awards.

Following the Emmy ceremony, HBO executive Casey Bloys sat down with Deadline and was asked for his thoughts on Apple TV+'s performance. Here's what he had to say:

DEADLINE: What are your thoughts on Apple TV+'s performance this time around? They became the most-awarded platform at the Emmys for the first time — do you have anything to say? BLOYS: To be honest, I'm actually thrilled, because I think they're strong competitors — Zack and Jamie. We've always had strong rivals — Showtime, FX, AMC, Netflix, Amazon — so Apple joining the fray has put everyone on their toes, and that's exactly when I perform at my best. They're a one-trillion-dollar company, so it's undoubtedly a big challenge, but we'll keep doing what we've always been doing — making the best programming possible.

Bloys joined HBO in 2004 and has been overseeing programming since 2016. His track record speaks for itself, and his response to Apple TV+'s wins was largely gracious and sincere, offering genuine congratulations.

However, the most interesting part of his response was this line: "They're a one-trillion-dollar company, so it's undoubtedly a big challenge."

We don't know Apple TV+'s internal budget, but there's no denying that Apple's overall financial resources far exceed those of most competitors, including HBO.

Coincidentally, Paramount is currently actively seeking to acquire HBO (along with other Warner Bros. Discovery assets) in hopes of competing more effectively with tech giants like Apple and Amazon.

Does scale naturally bring advantage? Perhaps. But plenty of networks have proven that, when it comes to making content audiences love, money is only a small part of the equation.

Apple TV+ costs $14.99 per month, and is also available as part of the Apple One subscription bundle.
